clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old woman presented with upper abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, consistent with small bowel obstruction (SBO). Imaging, including an abdominal series and CT scan, confirmed a partial SBO with a transition point at the terminal ileum and an adjacent soft-tissue nodule. Given her history of endometriosis, a diagnostic laparoscopy was performed, followed by a right hemicolectomy. Intraoperatively, a 2 cm ileal lesion and scattered adhesions involving the terminal ileum and right colon were noted. Pathology confirmed endometriosis involving the muscularis propria and serosa of the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and appendix, and explicitly identified a 1.8 × 1.5 × 1.1 endometrial mass as the cause of the SBO. Malignancy was ruled out. Specific evidence for endometriosis of the right round ligament was not explicitly documented beyond its mention in the final diagnosis.
